summary: Converts Python data (dataclasses, Pydantic models, dict-of-lists, list-of-dicts, named tuples, tuples, indexed data, Series dicts, collections) to a Polars DataFrame. PydataIngress.convert selects a handler through PydataIngressFactory and can apply a target TableSchema and an explicit source_table_schema; it also reports a compilation reuse descriptor for inline relation sources.
key_classes: PydataIngress — public entry; convert(data, table_schema, source_table_schema=, inline_conform=) -> Polars frame
PydataIngressFactory — BaseStrategyFactory that detects the data format and lazily loads a handler

DataframeFromDataclass / DataframeFromPydantic / DataframeFromPydict / DataframeFromPylist / DataframeFromNamedTuple / DataframeFromTuple / DataframeFromIndexedData / DataframeFromSeriesDict / IngressFromCollection / DataframeFromDefault — format handlers
key_functions: PydataIngress.convert(data, /, table_schema=None, *, source_table_schema=None, inline_conform=True) — convert Python data to a Polars DataFrame
repeatable_ingress_value(value) -> bool — decides whether an input is safe to reuse across compilations
lifecycle_notes: c1e8da53 and 22cc3292: source dtypes resolve per column (explicit source schema, then annotations, then bounded native inference).
a68147b6 removed transit policing; 838a285b shared schema declarations refactor.
documentation_hooks: Source schema vs target table_schema semantics
risks: Exports are lazy via lazy_loader, so names resolve only at attribute access.
table_schema is a conversion target and never source-type evidence; unrefined ANY is not an override.
Handler selection depends on data shape detection; ambiguous inputs fall to DataframeFromDefault.
